subject: Copywriting
title: Ogilvy's Long Copy
description: A quick, practical guide to Ogilvy's Long Copy.

hook.text: David Ogilvy believed long copy sold better than short. His Rolls-Royce ad had 607 words and sold out cars.

buildup.text: The headline: 'At 60 mph, the loudest noise comes from the electric clock.' Specific, factual, memorable.

discovery.text: Ogilvy's rule: every word must earn its place. Long copy isn't padding—it's more reasons to believe.

twist.text: Modern marketers say nobody reads long copy. Amazon product pages disagree. So do successful landing pages.

climax.text: Ogilvy proved that people read what interests them. Length matters less than relevance.

punchline.text: 607 words. Sold every car. Long copy isn't dead—boring copy is.

quiz.question: What was Ogilvy's famous Rolls-Royce headline about?
